item.subject: science
item.stem: In her science class in Jaipur, Meena learns that a human sperm cell and an egg cell each carry half the genetic material of a parent. Why does sexual reproduction not double the amount of genetic information in every new generation?

options.A: Each gamete carries half of a parent's genetic material, so joining two gametes restores the complete set of genetic instructions.
options.B: The parents give their complete genetic material to the offspring, so nothing is ever lost between generations.
options.C: Gametes from the two parents avoid mixing, so each offspring is an exact copy of only one parent.
options.D: Only one gamete takes part in fertilisation, so the genetic material stays the same.
